text_blocks.snippet: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) causes high blood pressure in the arteries of your lungs, forcing the right side of the heart to work harder to pump blood.
snippet_highlighted_words: high blood pressure in the arteries of your lungs

list.snippet: Shortness of breath (dyspnea), especially during physical activity like climbing stairs, exercising, or eventually while resting.
Dizziness or lightheadedness, which can lead to fainting (syncope).
Heart palpitations (a fast, pounding, or irregular heartbeat).
Edema (swelling in the feet, ankles, legs, and later in the abdomen or neck).
Cyanosis (bluish tint to the lips, skin, or fingers due to low oxygen).

text_blocks.snippet: PAH symptoms often start off mild or unnoticed during the early stages and mimic other heart or lung conditions. As outlined by the Cleveland Clinic, functional classes range from Class 1 (no symptoms during normal movement) to Class 4 (symptoms present even while resting).
More detailed guidance and resources are available through the American Lung Association.
